name: Monport GPro Vision 100W MOPA
tagline: Split MOPA fiber with 16 MP camera and autofocus: more power for deep engraving and relief
tldr: The GPro Vision 100W MOPA keeps the line's 16 MP camera, autofocus and 175 × 175 mm field with a 100W MOPA source for deeper engraving, 3D relief and thin-sheet cutting, alongside colour marking. $6,919.99 on Monport's store in October 2026, shown without a shipping delay. Launched in June 2026; no independent review yet.
mainObjective: Deep metal engraving and relief work with camera placement

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $6,919.99 machine only, $7,119.99 with LightBurn Pro

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cut: Thin steel, brass and copper sheet (many passes)
cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 175 × 175 mm field without repositioning

pros: Faster material removal for deep engraving, relief and embossing, with MOPA colour marking still available
Camera placement and autofocus for repeat parts and batch layouts
Shown without a shipping delay on Monport's store in October 2026
cons: $6,919.99: about $320 more than Monport's camera-less GT at the same power ($6,600)
No larger field than the cheaper MOPA tier: 175 × 175 mm
More heat on thin parts: colour work needs careful parameter tests

faq.question: GPro Vision 100W or GT 100W?
faq.answer: Both use a 100W MOPA source and autofocus. The GPro Vision 100W ($6,919.99, October 2026) adds the 16 MP camera and conveyor compatibility; the GT 100W was listed from $6,600. If you mark mostly flat stock positioned with jigs, the GT is enough; for varied finished parts, the camera earns its cost.

faq.question: What can the 100W MOPA do that the 60W cannot?
faq.answer: Nothing different in kind, but it does it faster: deeper engraving per pass, quicker 3D relief and embossing, and more practical cutting of thin steel or brass. Monport does not publish cutting thicknesses for this tier; expect thin sheet only, in many passes.

faq.question: Do I need an enclosure for the GPro Vision?
faq.answer: It is an open split galvo with a Class 4 beam. Monport includes OD7 glasses and sells an enclosure with a door safety switch ($509 in October 2026). In a shared room or a shop with visitors, the enclosure is the safer choice; fume extraction is also recommended for coated metals and plastics.

standoutFeatures.title: Depth and relief
standoutFeatures.body: The 100W MOPA source makes deep engraving, 3D embossing and thin-sheet cutting practical in production times, while keeping MOPA colour control.

standoutFeatures.title: Built for repeat production
standoutFeatures.body: Camera placement, autofocus and compatibility with Monport's conveyor accessory suit serialized parts and repeated logos.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 100W MOPA tier of the GPro Vision. Buy it when depth and throughput pay the bills; for colour and fine marking alone, compare the lower tiers via the chips.
proTips: Use several fast passes rather than one slow pass for deep engraving, to limit heat build-up and warping on thin parts. Keep the lens clean: at this power, dirt burns in quickly.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 100W tier suits shops that sell deep engraving, relief work, tool marking and small metal cut-outs, and want the camera to cut setup time on finished goods.
editorialDepth.limitations: The extra power costs about $1,600 over the cheaper MOPA tier with no larger field. It is more than colour-only or light marking work needs, and it still requires an enclosure or strict eye protection.
